item.title: 9/27 Potluck in the Park
item.description:

item.title: Support Your Beacon Hill Neighbor
item.description:
Support Your Neighbor Juan and his family

Cecilia, Juan, and their family are beloved neighbors in Beacon Hill. Since June 12th, Juan has been detained by ICE at the NW Detention Center, leaving Cecilia and their two children without a reliable source of income at home. Their children are students in Beacon Hill schools, and this family is also part of the local Catholic faith community. Right now, they are facing the pain and uncertainty of separation while also trying to keep daily life steady for their kids.

Support for this fundraiser will help Cecilia cover ongoing essentials like groceries, school supplies, and clothing for the growing kids. It will also help with licensing fees so the family can open their food truck and work toward more stability, along with legal expenses as Juan fights to stay with his family. Because these needs continue over time, recurring donations can make a real difference by helping Cecilia plan for regular household costs and the long legal process ahead. One-time donations are also deeply appreciated and will help meet immediate needs.

Donate here: https://www.gofundme.com/f/support-cecilia-juan-and-family

item.title: Potluck and Film 7/25 5pm-8pm
item.description:
We invite you all to our next potluck this evening which will be a film screening and discussion of Elements of Mutual Aid with the producers who are on a nationwide tour. We will be screening Chapter 2: Earth, please read the blurb below for more information or check out their website here. There will be Spanish subtitles available with the film. Kid friendly event.

This chapter takes a look at how to grow projects with strong, interconnected roots that can support communities. It explores how local needs and capacity should inform our projects, how we can network smaller projects over large areas, and how we can build infrastructure that outlasts crisis points. Meet a harm reduction project in Tucson, an international decentralized disaster response network, and a web of mutual aid centers in Puerto Rico.

Beacon Hill Community Potluck, Film Screening and Discussion

  • Potluck - 5pm - 8pm (ongoing)
  • Screening of Elements of Mutual Aid - 6pm-7pm (starts promptly)
  • Discussion with filmmakers - 7pm - 8pm

When: Saturday 7/25 5pm-8pm

Where: 1607 S Forest St What to bring: Food and drinks to share Access notes: There are stairs to access, please contact us if you need support with stairs - we want to support. Once inside the space, bathroom and area is accessible. Kid friendly (we'll have a kid zone with some activities but kids are welcome generally in the space too).

As always, feel free to drop in whenever, stay however long, and bring a friend or neighbor.

item.title: Potluck to Honor BHS Member and Neighbor Cristian Salyer
item.description:
We are deeply saddened to share that Beacon Hill Solidarity member, Cristian Salyer was killed in a traffic accident while biking this week. He had been contributing a lot of work to making our 6/16 potluck happen and you may have previously seen him at other BHS events - including frequently as our charismatic MC.

We would like to invite you all to come honor Cristian's life and memory with us tonight - whether you knew him as a friend, teacher, neighbor, musician or in any other walk of life. We'll hold a bonfire and share memories. Please bring what you can: food to share, flowers, pictures of Cristian, candles, and a blanket or extra chair if needed.

Please see the previous message below for the potluck details. We will still have an optional tenants rights workshop but it will be separate from our collective grieving space.

June Beacon Hill Community Potluck on Tuesday 6/16.

Join us to share food and enjoy the summer outside at the abundant Beacon Hill Food Forest. We are excited to host Puget Sound Tenants Union for a workshop on Tenants Rights for renters who may be experiencing problems with their landlord and are curious about how to leverage their own power. The workshop is optional and we will otherwise be eating food together and sharing in the beautiful garden space in our neighborhood.

When: Tuesday 6/16, 6:00PM-9:00pm

Where: Beacon Food Forest, located in Jefferson Park off South Dakota Street. We'll be meeting at the gathering space at the southeast end of the food forest (close to the parking lot). What to bring: A dish to share, chairs and blankets for sitting, your neighbors and especially fellow tenants if you're having problems with your landlord/housing situation Access notes: There's a parking lot on S Dakota; we also recommend walking, biking, or taking the bus (50, 60, and 107 stop right by the Food Forest on 15th). There is a gravel path to access the gathering space. This is an outdoor event! We'll have some shelter present in case of rain, but dress accordingly.

item.title: Community Potluck and Vigil
item.description:
Coming up next is the April Beacon Hill Community Potluck, which will also be a vigil space.

Join us as we gather on the evening before to collectively mourn, honor, and remember those we have lost. This is a space for all to be remembered and mourned. Bring photos, names, flowers, candles to contribute to the collective altar. Anyone is welcome to share a story, a poem, a song, etc. about someone meaningful to you who has died.

Where: Beacon Food Forest, located in Jefferson Park off South Dakota Street. We'll be meeting at the gathering space at the southeast end of the food forest (close to the parking lot). What to bring: A dish to share, chairs and blankets for sitting, flowers and items for the altar, layers or rain gear depending on weather Access notes: There's a parking lot on S Dakota; we also recommend walking, biking, or taking the bus (50, 60, and 107 stop right by the Food Forest on 15th). There is a gravel path to access the gathering space. This is an outdoor event! We'll have some shelter present in case of rain, but dress accordingly.

Together, we will help each other honor the dead, so that we may continue to fight for the living.

item.title: Support Beacon Hill Neighbor José and his family
item.description:
As many of you may know, ICE kidnapped one of our Beacon Hill neighbors, José, who runs the El Saborcito taco truck, located in the parking lot of the Dino Mart gas station at Beacon Ave S and S Steven St. José is being detained in Texas. As of 1/29, his court hearing was canceled because they have already filed the necessary paperwork with the federal judge. Now we are just waiting for the judge to issue the order for his release, and José will hopefully soon return to his family and Beacon Hill.

More information about José's situation can be found in the flyer at the end of this email. Please help share and donate to this existing fundraiser, which will help cover legal and family expenses.

Link to donate here: https://www.gofundme.com/f/jose-and-el-saborcito

item.title: Support Beacon Hill families recovering from fire
item.description:
On Sunday, January 11th 2026, an apartment fire at the Olympic View Manor destroyed/damaged multiple units and impacted many families and residents. A month later, the GoFundMe fundraiser for supporting the impacted families and neighbors has reached about 50% of its goal of $45k. Donations support families with needs including emergency housing, purchasing necessities, financial help with relocating and legal support, and more.

Link to GoFundMe: https://www.gofundme.com/f/help-beacon-hill-families-after-apartment-fire

Please continue helping to circulate the fundraiser and consider donating!
